_comment: Audit I-02 / A-06 — the service page template's content. H1 follows the pattern '<Service> for <building types> in <region>'; the equipment list moves to the subhead, where it belongs. Every claim here is supported by the project pages in projects.json. `relatedProjects` must be real project ids.

hvac.h1: Commercial HVAC installation and service for schools and commercial buildings in Metro Vancouver
hvac.promise: Rooftop units, make-up air, air handlers, classroom unit ventilators, heat pumps and VRF — installed around the people still using the building.
hvac.subhead: RTU, MUA, AHU, unit ventilators, heat pumps and VRF, with DDC integration to Delta, Reliable and Trane.
hvac.alt: Rooftop air handling unit being serviced on a school roof

audiences.title: School districts
audiences.copy: Classroom ventilation upgrades delivered in term time, phased so teaching continues. Districts 40, 43, 45 and 48.

audiences.title: Strata and property managers
audiences.copy: Make-up air, corridor pressurisation and suite heat pumps in occupied residential buildings.

audiences.title: Commercial buildings and GCs
audiences.copy: Rooftop and air handling replacements coordinated with tenants, trades and the consultant's schedule.

deliver: Rooftop unit, make-up air unit and air handler replacement and retrofit
Classroom unit ventilators, including removal of existing convectors and coils
Heat pumps and VRF multi-zone systems
Hydronic connections, circulator pumps and piping to existing systems
Seismic restraint, housekeeping pads and associated carpentry
Air balance, performance verification and commissioning coordination
hvac.equipment: We work to the consultant's equipment schedule. Controls integration is usually Delta, Reliable or Trane DDC, with trending and alarms set up at handover.

steps.title: Site review
steps.copy: We walk the mechanical rooms and the affected spaces, confirm what is actually installed, and agree access windows.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.copy: A written scope with the equipment, the sequence and the phasing, priced against the drawings or against what we found on site.

steps.title: Shop drawings and submittals
steps.copy: Equipment submittals and shop drawings through the engineer, with lead times confirmed before anything is ordered.

steps.title: Install around occupancy
steps.copy: Evenings, weekends or term breaks where the space has to stay in use. Trade coordination with electrical, sheet metal, controls and insulation.

steps.title: Commissioning and turnover
steps.copy: Air balance, verification, O&M manuals, as-builts and a walkthrough with the people who will operate it.

boilers.h1: Boiler plant replacement and heating service for schools, strata and commercial buildings in Metro Vancouver
boilers.promise: Condensing plants swapped into live buildings — sized, piped, controlled and commissioned without losing a heating season.
boilers.subhead: Condensing boilers, burners, VFD pumps, heat exchangers, tanks, safety devices and controls.
boilers.serviceType: Commercial boiler plant replacement and heating service
boilers.alt: Bank of condensing boilers in a school mechanical room

audiences.title: School districts
audiences.copy: Plant replacements sequenced around the school year. At Ridgeview we installed six IBC boilers alongside a classroom ventilation conversion.

audiences.title: Strata and apartment buildings
audiences.copy: Heating and domestic hot water plants in buildings that cannot go cold — a 2.5 million BTU Viessmann plant at 1755 Haro Street.

audiences.title: Commercial and institutional owners
audiences.copy: Plant modernisation tied into existing hydronics and building automation, as at the ICBC facility on West 5th.

deliver: Condensing boiler plant replacement, including removal of redundant equipment
Hydronic piping, circulation pumps, heat exchangers and expansion equipment
Gas distribution, venting and condensate management
Pre-operational cleaning, chemical treatment and water-system balancing
Direct digital control upgrades and HVAC system verification
Seismic restraint, concrete housekeeping pads and remediation
boilers.equipment: We install IBC, Viessmann, Rinnai and Daikin equipment, and whatever else the specification calls for. Controls work is typically Delta, Reliable or Trane.

steps.title: Site review
steps.copy: Existing plant condition, flue routes, gas capacity, electrical supply and how much room there really is to get equipment in and out.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.copy: Scope, equipment, the shutdown window required and what temporary heat, if any, the building needs.

steps.title: Submittals and procurement
steps.copy: Boiler and pump submittals through the engineer. Compatibility between proposed operating temperatures and existing coils is confirmed before order.

steps.title: Changeover
steps.copy: The plant comes out and goes in inside the agreed window, with gas, venting, controls and electrical coordinated to one sequence.

steps.title: Commissioning and turnover
steps.copy: Cleaning, treatment, balancing, verification, O&M manuals and as-builts, then a handover with the operating team.

commercial-plumbing.h1: Commercial and institutional plumbing for schools, strata and commercial buildings in Metro Vancouver
commercial-plumbing.promise: Risers, plants and fixtures in buildings that stay occupied — planned around shutdown notices, not around us.
commercial-plumbing.subhead: Backflow prevention, PRVs, booster pumps, domestic hot water plants, riser work and tenant improvements.
commercial-plumbing.alt: Copper and press-fit plumbing risers in a commercial washroom

audiences.title: Schools and public buildings
audiences.copy: Washroom renewals, domestic water and drainage work scheduled against the school calendar.

audiences.title: Strata and apartment buildings
audiences.copy: Riser replacement, domestic hot water plants and booster sets, with resident notice periods built into the plan.

audiences.title: Commercial landlords and GCs
audiences.copy: Tenant improvements, backflow testing and PRV stations, coordinated with building operations.

deliver: Backflow prevention installation and testing
Pressure reducing valve stations and booster pump sets
Domestic hot water plants and recirculation
Riser, main and branch replacement in copper and press-fit
Fixture replacement and tenant improvement rough-in
Drainage, venting and sanitary work
commercial-plumbing.equipment: Material and fixture selection follows the specification. Where there is none, we propose what we would install in our own building and tell you why.

steps.title: Site review
steps.copy: What is installed now, where the isolation points are, and which parts of the building each shutdown affects.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.copy: Scope and sequence, with the shutdown windows and notice periods stated up front.

steps.title: Notices and coordination
steps.copy: We work with the building manager on resident or tenant notices, access and temporary provisions.

steps.title: Execution
steps.copy: Work done in the agreed windows, with the system back in service at the end of each one wherever possible.

steps.title: Turnover
steps.copy: Testing records, as-builts and the documentation the building team needs for its own records.

maintenance.h1: Preventive maintenance programs for schools, strata and commercial buildings in Metro Vancouver
maintenance.promise: A scheduled visit, a written report and a recommendation list you can budget against — instead of a call-out at 2 am.
maintenance.subhead: Monthly, quarterly and annual programs with equipment checks, DDC trend reviews and reporting.
maintenance.alt: Technician checking a mechanical room equipment list on a tablet

audiences.title: School districts
audiences.copy: Multi-site programs across a district's buildings, with one report format and one point of contact.

audiences.title: Strata councils
audiences.copy: Boiler, domestic hot water and ventilation equipment on a schedule the council can plan reserves against.

audiences.title: Property and facility managers
audiences.copy: Equipment lists kept current, so a failure is a known risk rather than a surprise.

deliver: Scheduled visits — monthly, quarterly or annual, set per equipment list
Boiler, pump, air handling and ventilation equipment checks
DDC trend review, alarm history and setpoint verification
Water treatment checks and filter programs
A written report after each visit, with recommendations and priorities
Service history kept against each piece of equipment
maintenance.equipment: The equipment list is agreed at the start and kept current as things are replaced, so the report always matches the building.

steps.title: Equipment survey
steps.copy: We walk the building and build the list: make, model, capacity, age and condition.

steps.title: Program proposal
steps.copy: Visit frequency and scope per equipment type, priced annually so it fits a budget cycle.

steps.title: First visit
steps.copy: A baseline condition report — this is usually where deferred items surface.

steps.title: Ongoing visits
steps.copy: Scheduled work, with a report and a recommendation list after each one.

steps.title: Annual review
steps.copy: What changed, what is coming due, and what should be in next year's capital plan.

emergency.h1: 24/7 emergency plumbing, heating and HVAC service across Metro Vancouver
emergency.promise: No heat, a leak, a flood or a plant failure. One number, answered any hour.
emergency.subhead: Call 604-731-1000. For a gas smell, leave the building first and call FortisBC on 1-800-663-9911.
emergency.alt: Allied service van at night with a technician working by flashlight

audiences.title: Schools
audiences.copy: A plant failure before a school day is a different problem from one on a Saturday. Tell us which it is.

audiences.title: Strata and apartment buildings
audiences.copy: No heat or no hot water across a building, and leaks that affect more than one suite.

audiences.title: Commercial buildings
audiences.copy: Plant failures, floods and anything that is about to stop the building being usable.

deliver: No heat and no hot water across a building
Leaks, burst pipes and flooding
Boiler plant and pump failures
Rooftop and air handling unit failures
Drain blockages affecting occupied space
Temporary provisions while a permanent repair is arranged
emergency.equipment: Tell the dispatcher the building address, what has failed and who is on site. That is usually enough to send the right person with the right parts.

steps.title: Call, do not email
steps.copy: 604-731-1000 is answered around the clock. A form sits in an inbox until someone opens it.

steps.title: Make it safe
steps.copy: If you can reach the isolation valve or the main shut-off safely, close it. For a gas smell, leave the building and call FortisBC.

steps.title: We attend
steps.copy: Timing depends on your location, the failure and who is available. The dispatcher will tell you what to expect.

steps.title: Stabilise
steps.copy: Get the building usable — a temporary provision now, with the permanent repair scheduled properly.

steps.title: Follow up
steps.copy: A written note of what failed and what we recommend, so it can go into the maintenance plan.

residential-plumbing.h1: Residential plumbing, heating and hot water across Metro Vancouver
residential-plumbing.promise: Repairs, replacements and repipes, done tidily and explained in plain language.
residential-plumbing.subhead: Repairs, fixture replacements, rough-ins, repipes, and tank and tankless water heaters.
residential-plumbing.alt: Plumber fitting a fixture in a residential bathroom

audiences.title: Homeowners
audiences.copy: Repairs, fixture replacements and water heaters, with the work and the price agreed before it starts.

audiences.title: Apartment residents
audiences.copy: In-suite work, coordinated with your building manager where a shut-off affects neighbours.

audiences.title: Renovations
audiences.copy: Rough-in and finish plumbing for bathroom and kitchen work, scheduled around the other trades.

deliver: Repairs to supply, drainage and venting
Fixture replacement and installation
Rough-in for renovations and additions
Repipes in PEX and copper
Tank and tankless water heater replacement
Gas fitting for appliances and heating equipment
residential-plumbing.equipment: Tankless and tank water heaters from Rinnai and others. We will tell you honestly when a repair is the better call than a replacement.

steps.title: Tell us what is happening
steps.copy: Where it is, what it does, and how long it has done it. Photos help more than you would think.

steps.title: Attend and diagnose
steps.copy: We confirm the cause before quoting a fix, so you are not paying for guesswork.

steps.title: Agree the work
steps.copy: A price for the work itself, and a clear answer on whether repair or replacement makes more sense.

steps.title: Do the work
steps.copy: Isolation, the work, testing, and the site left clean.

steps.title: Hand over
steps.copy: How to operate anything new, and what to watch for.
